title: Daily Kidney Quiz
description: 3 quick, bite-sized questions to reinforce what you learned today.

questions.question: What is the primary function of your kidneys?
options: Filtering waste and water from the blood
questions.explanation: Kidneys clean your blood continuously and balance essential salts and water.

questions.question: What is the recommended maximum daily salt intake for UK adults?
questions.explanation: 6 grams of salt (or 2,400mg sodium) is the NHS daily maximum.

questions.question: Which common painkiller should generally be checked with your pharmacist if you have CKD?
questions.explanation: NSAIDs like ibuprofen can reduce blood flow into the kidney filters.

title: Salt Detective
description: Compare two packaged foods and spot the lower-salt choice.

scenarios.title: Lunchtime Soup Choice
scenarios.prompt: Which soup is the kidney-friendly, lower-salt option?
scenarios.tip: Canned and instant soups often contain over 25% of your entire daily salt allowance in a single bowl.

scenarios.title: Breakfast Choice

itemB.name: Smoked Bacon Sandwich with Brown Sauce

scenarios.prompt: Which breakfast protects your blood pressure target best?
scenarios.tip: Smoked and cured meats are very high in sodium. Plain oats have virtually zero added salt.

title: Pill Check
description: Learn which over-the-counter medicines need a pharmacist check.

items.reason: NSAID painkillers can reduce blood flow into the kidneys and trigger acute kidney strain.
Paracetamol is generally safe for kidneys when taken according to package instructions.
These products replace sodium with high levels of potassium, which kidneys may struggle to clear.
Unregulated herbal extracts can contain heavy metals or compounds that irritate kidney filters.

title: Sick-Day Rules Card Sort
description: Drag medicines into 'Pause during severe vomiting/diarrhoea' or 'Usually continue'.

cards.name: Ramipril (ACE Inhibitor)
cards.reason: Blood pressure drops during dehydration; pausing prevents kidney strain.

cards.name: Losartan (ARB)
cards.reason: Protective in health, but pause during severe dehydrating illness.

cards.name: Furosemide (Water Pill / Diuretic)
cards.reason: Losing more fluid when already dehydrated causes acute injury.

cards.name: Paracetamol (for fever)
cards.reason: Helps control high temperature without dropping renal blood flow.

cards.name: Thyroxine (Thyroid tablet)
cards.reason: Standard hormone replacement that does not affect fluid balance.

readings.note: Worth discussing with your GP surgery.

title: Lab Results Decoder
description: Understand what eGFR and urine ACR numbers really mean.

pairs.meaning: Stage G2: Mild reduction; kidneys still doing a great job filtering.
Stage G3a: Mild-moderate reduction; routine 6-monthly reviews recommended.
Stage A1: Normal protein; kidney filters are keeping protein sealed inside.
Stage A2: Microalbuminuria; tiny protein leaks showing mild filter strain.

title: Kidney Quest: A Day in the Life
description: Make healthy, realistic choices in a short interactive daily story.

steps.prompt: You wake up feeling a bit rushed before work. What is a kidney-friendly way to start the day?

choices.text: A tall glass of water and a warm bowl of porridge with berries
choices.feedback: Excellent! Hydrating and gentle on blood pressure with zero added salt.

choices.text: Skip breakfast and grab two salty bacon rolls on the run
choices.feedback: High in salt, which pulls blood pressure up throughout the morning.
